entries.title: Change the Netgear Wi-Fi password
entries.summary: Log in to the router at routerlogin.net, open the wireless settings, type a new password for both bands, and reconnect each device. About 20 minutes.

details.Time: About 20 minutes, plus reconnecting each device
details.You need: A laptop or phone, ideally a laptop with an Ethernet cable

body.text: First, which box is which

Mom's setup has three Netgear boxes. The tall black one with the triangle-hole pattern and the round cable screwed into the back is the cable modem. It brings the internet in and has no Wi-Fi of its own, so you never change the Wi-Fi password on it.

The Wi-Fi comes from a router. There are two: the smaller, older one with the round blue button on top (its sticker says N600, model WNDR3400v2), and the flat router with three antennas (a Nighthawk-style model; its model number wasn't visible in the photos). In the photos the older N600 had its lights on and a yellow cable running to it, so it's most likely the one making the Wi-Fi. That's a guess from photos, so check which one has its lights on before you start.
If both routers are plugged in and lit, they may each broadcast their own network. Change the password on every router that's on, or unplug the one you don't use.
Change the Wi-Fi password

items: Connect to the router. A laptop plugged into one of the numbered LAN ports with an Ethernet cable is best, because Wi-Fi devices drop off the moment the password changes. A phone or laptop already on Mom's Wi-Fi also works.
Open a web browser and go to www.routerlogin.net. If that doesn't load, type 192.168.1.1 instead.
Sign in. The user name is admin. The password is the router's admin password, which is different from the Wi-Fi password. If nobody ever changed it, Netgear's factory default is the word password.
Open the wireless settings. On most Netgear routers it's under BASIC, then Wireless. On older models like the N600 it can appear as Wireless Settings in the left menu.
Under Security Options, choose WPA2-PSK [AES], or WPA2/WPA3 if your router offers it.
Type the new password in the Password (Network Key) box. Dual-band routers show one box for 2.4 GHz and one for 5 GHz; fill in both. Using the same password for both is fine.
Click Apply and wait about a minute. Every Wi-Fi device will disconnect.
Reconnect each device using the new password: phones, laptops, TV, printer, smart speakers.

body.text: Pick a password Mom can actually type

Three or four unrelated words plus a two-digit number make a strong password that's still easy to type on a TV remote. Aim for at least 12 characters. Write it on a card and keep it in a drawer, not taped to the router.
When a laptop says the password isn't correct

Windows remembers the old password and keeps trying it. Open Settings, then Network & internet, then Wi-Fi, then Manage known networks. Pick Mom's network, choose Forget, then connect again and type the new password carefully. Watch for capital letters; the password is case-sensitive. On an iPhone, open Settings, then Wi-Fi, tap the (i) next to the network and choose Forget This Network.
Then change the router's admin password

The admin password protects the settings page. If it's still the factory word, anyone on the Wi-Fi could change Mom's settings. On most Netgear routers it's under ADVANCED, then Administration, then Set Password. Type the current one, then the new one twice.
If you can't log in

If the admin password was changed and nobody remembers it, the fix is a factory reset. With the router on, press and hold the small recessed reset button (labeled Restore Factory Settings on the N600) with a paperclip for about seven seconds, until the power light blinks. That timing is typical for Netgear routers; check your model's manual if it doesn't work. A reset erases every setting: the Wi-Fi name and password go back to what's printed on the sticker, and the admin login goes back to admin and password. Then follow the steps above to set new ones.
Keep passwords out of photos, texts and chats. The router stickers and some earlier photos show passwords, which is one more reason to change them now.
Worth knowing

The N600 (WNDR3400v2) is an older model. Netgear stops sending security updates when a product reaches End of Service, and older models like this one are likely past that point. Check its status at netgear.com/about/eos. If the three-antenna router is newer and works, using it instead of the N600 is the safer choice.

entries.title: Hang the big frames in the living room
entries.summary: Weigh each frame, decide between the wall and the wood beam, then use hooks rated for the weight. Two hooks per wide frame keeps it level.

details.Time: About an hour for two frames
details.Cost: About $15 to $40 in hooks and anchors
details.You need: Bathroom scale, tape measure, pencil, level, drill, stud finder
details.Where: Living room wall or the dark wood beam

body.text: The photos show two large framed pieces with picture wire across the back, a dark wood beam running along the top of the wall, and a ceiling hook holding a hanging shell decoration on chain and S-hooks.

items: Weigh each frame. Step on a bathroom scale holding it, then subtract your own weight.
Choose hardware rated for at least twice the frame's weight. The rating is printed on the package.
For frames wider than about two feet, use two hooks spaced apart instead of one. The frame stays level and the weight is shared.
Find a stud with a stud finder if you can. A screw into a stud holds far more than drywall alone.
Mark the height. A common guide is the center of the art about 57 to 60 inches from the floor, or 6 to 10 inches above a sofa.
Pull the picture wire up tight toward the top with a finger, measure from the top of the frame to the wire's peak, and set the hooks that far below your top-edge mark.
Hang it, step back, and check it with a level.

body.text: Hanging from the wood beam

Some beams are solid wood and some are hollow decorative boxes. Knock along it: a dull, solid thud means real wood; a hollow drum sound means a cover. A solid beam takes a screw-in eye hook or cup hook in a pre-drilled pilot hole. Don't hang heavy frames or mirrors from a hollow beam.
The ceiling hook

A screw hook in the ceiling should go into a joist or use a toggle bolt rated for the weight. Textured drywall on its own holds very little, so check that the existing hook is snug before adding anything to the chain.
Mirrors are heavier than they look. If a mirror is over about 30 pounds, use D-rings on the frame and a French cleat or screws into studs instead of a single wire.

entries.title: Put up the folding door in the bathroom doorway
entries.summary: Take down the old swinging door, screw the track to the top of the frame, hang the folding door on it, then fix one edge to the side of the frame. About an hour with a helper.

details.Time: About 1 hour, plus 15 minutes to take down the old door
details.Cost: Door already bought; nothing else needed
details.Skill: Beginner, with a helper for the old door
details.You need: Small Phillips screwdriver, tape measure, drill with a 3/32-inch bit or a small nail, hacksaw or fine-tooth saw, masking tape, safety glasses, step stool
details.The door: Spectrum Via folding door, white, for openings up to 36 inches wide and 80 inches high

body.text: Mom bought a Spectrum Via folding door in white. It's a vinyl accordion door that comes with its own top track, handles, magnetic latch and screws. The box says it fits openings up to 36 inches wide and 80 inches high, and the store listings for this size say 24 to 36 inches wide. Mom's bathroom doorway measured roughly 28 to 29 inches, so it should fit.
These steps follow the maker's instructions (LTL Home Products) for their 24 to 36 inch folding doors. Read the sheet inside Mom's box first; if any step differs, follow her sheet.
See the illustrated step-by-step
Before you start

items: Open the box and check the parts: the folded door, the top track, two handles with two small pins, track screws, anchor screws with washers, the magnetic latch plate with its small screws, and a packet of lubricant.
Measure the width inside the door frame, from one side of the frame to the other, at the top. Write it down. It must be 36 inches or less.
Measure the height from the floor to the underside of the top of the frame, on both sides. Use the smaller number.

body.text: Take down the old swinging door

items: Close the door most of the way and have your helper hold it steady by the knob.
Tap each hinge pin up and out with a screwdriver and hammer, working upward from underneath. Do the bottom hinge first and the top hinge last.
Lift the door away and lean it somewhere safe. Keep the door and pins in case Mom ever wants it back.
Unscrew the hinge plates left on the frame so the folding door can sit flat against that side. Keep the screws with the old door.

body.text: Put up the folding door

items: Trim if needed. If the opening is shorter than about 80 inches, tape the folded panels together and saw the extra off the bottom (the end without holes). Then cut the top track 1/8 inch shorter than the width you measured.

Fit the track. Hold it centered against the underside of the top of the frame. Make a small pilot hole through the hole nearest the middle of the track with a nail or the 3/32-inch bit, and drive one track screw there. Leave it loose so the track can swing.

Attach the handles. Tap the two pins into one handle, push the pins through the holes in the door edge, and press the second handle onto them from the other side. Tap around the pins, never on the middle of the handle.

Hang the door. Put a little of the lubricant on each roller at the top of the door. Swing one end of the track down and out of the opening, decide which side the door should open from, and slide all the rollers onto the track. Push the folded door toward the middle screw.
Fix the track. Swing it back into place, make pilot holes, and drive a screw through every track hole. Keep each screw straight and tight so the door glides smoothly.

Fix the anchor edge. Slide the whole door to the side where the old hinges were. Let it hang straight, then put the anchor screws through the washers and the three holes in that edge panel and into the frame.

Fit the latch. Close the door until its edge meets the other side of the frame. Mark where the magnetic latch plate lines up with the metal strip on the door edge, and screw it to the frame with the small flathead screws.
Test it. Open and close it a few times using the handle. It should glide without catching and click shut on the magnet.

body.text: Always open and close it by the handle. Pushing on the end of the folding door can pinch fingers against the frame. Wear safety glasses when sawing or drilling overhead.

A folding door closes with a magnet and doesn't lock. If Mom wants privacy with guests, a small hook-and-eye latch on the inside is an easy add-on. The old hinge holes can be filled with wood filler and touched up with white paint whenever there's time.

entries.title: Fit a better gate in the bathroom doorway
entries.summary: Measure the opening at three heights, then choose a walk-through gate with a latch so Mom never has to step over it.

details.Cost: Roughly $30 to $90 for a walk-through gate

body.text: Mom has since bought a Spectrum Via folding door for this doorway. See "Put up the folding door in the bathroom doorway" for the steps. The measuring steps below still apply.
The photos show a white plastic pet gate set in the bathroom doorway, with the dogs inside, and the opening being measured across and up the door frame.
One photo reads roughly 28 to 29 inches across, but it's hard to tell which edge the tape started from. Re-measure before buying.

items: Measure between the door jambs, inside the frame, not across the decorative trim.
Measure at the bottom, middle and top. Use the smallest number.
Check which way the door swings so the gate won't stop it from closing.
Choose a gate whose fit range includes your number, with room to spare on both ends.
Pick a walk-through style with a latch. Stepping over a gate is a common way to trip and fall.
For a pressure-mounted gate, use the wall cups that come with it on painted trim so it doesn't slide or mark the paint.

body.text: If the goal is to keep dogs out while still letting air and light in, a walk-through gate is the quick fix. Converting the door into a half door is a much bigger project.

entries.title: Sand and refinish the carved front door
entries.summary: Test for lead first, sand the flat parts with a sander and the carvings by hand, then seal with an exterior finish that blocks UV.

details.You need: Lead test kit, sander, sanding sponges, brushes, exterior stain and UV-blocking clear coat
details.Where: Front door, in shade, early in the day

body.text: The photos show a solid wood front door with fifteen carved panels and cream-colored accents. The hinge side is sun-bleached and dry, with raised grain where the finish has worn off.

If the house was built before 1978, old paint or finish may contain lead. Test the cream accents and the finish with a lead test kit from a hardware store before any sanding. If it tests positive, don't dry-sand; hire a lead-safe certified painter.

items: Take off or tape over the lever handle and deadbolt.
Wash the door with mild soap and water, rinse, and let it dry completely.
Sand the flat rails and stiles with an orbital sander, starting at 120 grit and finishing at 180.
Sand the carvings by hand with flexible sanding sponges or folded sandpaper. Power sanders round over carved edges.
Clean dust out of the carvings with a soft brush, then wipe with a tack cloth.
Touch up the cream accents with a small artist's brush and exterior paint, if needed.
Apply an exterior stain to even out the faded side, following the can's dry time.
Finish with two or three thin coats of an exterior clear coat with UV blockers, such as spar urethane. Lightly sand between coats with very fine paper.

body.text: Desert sun breaks down door finishes fast. Plan a light maintenance coat on the sunny side every year or two, and work in the shade so the finish doesn't dry before you can brush it out.

entries.title: Paver patio with benches and a fire pit
entries.summary: A weekend build: grey pavers on leveled sand, a white pebble border, cinder-block-and-cedar benches, and a fire pit in the middle.

details.You need: Shovel, landscape fabric, leveling sand, straight board, rubber mallet
details.Where: Backyard, about a 10 by 10 foot area

items: Mark the footprint, strip the grass and dig down a few inches.
Lay landscape fabric over the whole area.
Spread leveling sand and drag a straight board across it until flat.
Set 24-inch pavers in a grid and tap each one level.
Paint the border blocks charcoal and set them around the edge.
Fill the channel between pavers and border with white pebbles.
Stack cinder blocks and slide cedar 4x4s through them for benches.
Add the fire pit, potted lavender and a lantern.

body.text: From Mom's Backyard Hub plan. Check local rules on open fires before using the fire pit.

entries.title: Gilded hands planter
entries.summary: Two concrete hands cast in rubber gloves cradle a bowl molded in a watermelon, all sprayed metallic gold and planted with flowers.

details.Time: One weekend with an overnight cure
details.You need: Rubber gloves, concrete mix, a watermelon, a small steel bowl, gold spray paint

items: Fill two rubber gloves with quick-set concrete and hang them to set in a relaxed shape.
Cut and peel the gloves away once firm.
Use a hollowed watermelon half as the bowl mold, with a small steel bowl pressed in to leave a planting cavity.
Peel off the rind once cured.
Set the bowl into the cupped hands.
Spray everything metallic gold, then plant it.

body.text: From Mom's Backyard Hub. This idea came from a social media screenshot; expect some trial and error with the glove casts.

entries.title: Hand-poured stone vessel sink
entries.summary: A scalloped concrete bowl cast over an open umbrella, with a white basin and a ring of red glass pebbles. Works indoors as a sink or outdoors as a fountain bowl.

details.You need: Umbrella, concrete mix, plastic tub, masonry bit, sink-rated paint, drain kit, faucet

items: Pour concrete over an open, braced umbrella to form the scalloped bowl.
Set a round plastic tub in the center and pour around it to form the basin.
Press pebbles into the wet rim.
Lift out the tub once cured, then drill the drain hole.
Seal and paint the basin white, set the glass pebble ring, and fit the drain and faucet.

body.text: Concrete must be fully sealed before it holds water indoors, and connecting a new sink is plumbing work. If it's going in a bathroom, have a plumber connect it.

entries.title: Sculpted concrete bear table
entries.summary: A large plush bear coated in concrete, posed with arms up, painted and sealed, with a round glass top on its paws.

details.Cost: About $330 to $530 plus mixer rental (estimated August 2026)
details.You need: Large plush bear, 15 to 20 bags of concrete, rented mixer, props, exterior paint, sealer, glass top

body.text: The biggest of the four backyard ideas: coat the bear in concrete, brace the pose while it cures, smooth it, paint the face and details, seal it, and set a glass top cut to size on the paws.
This technique comes from a social media video and hasn't been tested here. The finished piece will be very heavy; plan who moves it and where it lives before casting.

entries.title: Swap a light fixture for a ceiling fan
entries.summary: Six steps in an afternoon. The one check that matters: the ceiling box must be rated for a fan, not just for weight.

details.Cost: Cost of the fan, plus a fan-rated brace if needed
details.You need: Non-contact voltage tester, screwdrivers, wire strippers, ladder, helper

items: Turn off the breaker, not just the wall switch, and confirm with a voltage tester.
Take down the old fixture and photograph the wiring.
Check the ceiling box is stamped as fan-rated. If not, install a fan-rated brace.
Mount the fan bracket.
Wire the motor, attach the blades and balance them.
Turn the breaker on and test the fan, light and remote.

body.text: Some cities require a permit for fixture changes. A quick call to the local building department settles it.

entries.title: Strip paint off hinges and polish them
entries.summary: Remove dried paint overspray from hinges and hardware with Goof Off, then polish brass with Brasso and nickel with Bar Keepers Friend.

details.You need: Goof Off Pro Strength, Brasso, Bar Keepers Friend, rags, gloves, goggles

items: Test the remover on a hidden spot of one hinge and wait a minute.
Dampen a rag with remover rather than pouring it on the metal.
Wipe off the paint one hinge at a time.
Polish brass with Brasso and nickel or chrome with Bar Keepers Friend.
Rinse, dry and reinstall.

body.text: Goof Off is very flammable. Work outside, away from pilot lights and heaters, with gloves and eye protection.

entries.title: Paint a textured door without losing the texture
entries.summary: Normal paint follows the wood-grain texture instead of filling it. Clean first, use thin coats, and don't sand aggressively.

details.Cost: About $30 to $60 in paint and supplies
details.You need: Mild cleaner, light sanding sponge, primer if needed, brush and small roller

body.text: A coat of latex paint is a thin film, so wood-grain lines and panel edges stay visible. Texture is only lost by heavy sanding, filler, skim coats or thick high-build primers.

items: Clean the door with mild soap or a TSP substitute and let it dry.
Scuff gloss lightly with a fine sanding sponge, without flattening the grain.
Prime only if changing from dark to light or covering stains.
Brush the panel edges first, then roll the flat areas with thin coats.

entries.title: Seal cracks in a roof parapet
entries.summary: Clean, fill and seal each crack early in the morning, then topcoat with elastomeric roof coating once the sealant has cured.

details.Time: About two hours for sealing, plus a topcoat later
details.Cost: Depends on the number of cracks
details.You need: Wire brush, elastomeric caulk or Sashco Mor-Flexx, backer rod, gloves, eye protection

body.text: Hairline cracks get one bead of elastomeric caulk tooled flush. Wider cracks get packed first, then bridged with sealant. Where loose stucco has come off down to block, a flexible mortar repair product like Sashco Mor-Flexx fills it.
Work before late morning in summer heat. Wear grippy shoes, bring water, set the ladder on level ground, and tell someone you're on the roof.

entries.title: Magnetic dryer vent connector
entries.summary: A wall bracket and hose collar with magnets, so the dryer hose pops off by hand for cleaning.

details.Where: Laundry room, standard 4-inch duct (done for Kat)

items: Screw the wall plate around the existing vent opening.
Seat the wall-side collar in the bracket.
Fit the hose-side magnetic ring to the dryer hose.
Snap the two together and check for a snug seal.

body.text: Cleaning lint from the vent regularly lowers dryer fire risk. This kit makes that a quick job.

entries.title: Wasps at a damaged roof vent
entries.summary: Never seal a vent wasps are using. Confirm whether there's an active nest first, treat it if there is, then replace the vent cap and screen.

details.Cost: About $15 for a vent repair to $400 or more if a nest needs treatment (estimated September 2026)
details.You need: Safe viewing distance, a pest professional's opinion
details.Where: Flat roof exhaust vent (done for Kat)

items: Watch the vent from a distance for a few minutes. Steady traffic in and out suggests an active nest.
Have an experienced person confirm what's inside without disturbing it.
If there's a nest, have it treated and let it clear completely.
Then replace the torn screen and cracked hood.

body.text: Sealing a vent with a live nest inside can push wasps through drywall or ducts into the house.
